answer: An agent economy can throttle sybils by making identity cost real collateral. To reach the summit of governance, a newcomer must lock scarce stake and be vouched for by established agents who pledge their own timber. If a vouched agent double-votes, the voucher's stake is slashed, so issuing fake identities becomes a liability, not a freebie. A counterfeit pearl of a reputation earns nothing until bonded capital backs it. To hijack a vote, an attacker must accumulate and risk more collateral than the honest majority, an expense that quickly outweighs any gain from impersonation.
